'''Michel Bierlaire''' (born 9 February 1967) is a Belgian-Swiss applied mathematician specialising in transportation systems. He is Professor of Operations Research at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL) and directs the university’s Transport and Mobility Laboratory.<ref name="EPFL-TML">{{cite web |title=Transport and Mobility Laboratory |url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/transp-or/ |website=EPFL |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref>

==Education==
Bierlaire studied mathematics at the [[University of Namur]], obtaining his PhD in 1996 for research on transportation-demand models supervised by Philippe Toint.<ref name="EPFL-people" />

==Career==
From 1995 to 1998 he was a research associate in the Intelligent Transportation Systems Program at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he co-developed '''DynaMIT''', a real-time traffic-prediction tool.<ref>{{cite conference |first1=Moshe |last1=Ben-Akiva |first2=Michel |last2=Bierlaire |first3=Haris |last3=Koutsopoulos |first4=Rabi |last4=Mishalani |title=DynaMIT: A Simulation-Based System for Traffic Prediction |conference=Short-Term Forecasting Workshop, DACCORD |year=1998 |url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/117145 |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref> Bierlaire joined EPFL in 1998 as a senior scientist, became Associate Professor in 2006 and Full Professor in 2012.<ref name="EPFL-people" /> He founded the Transport and Mobility Laboratory in 2006<ref name="EPFL-TML" /> and directed EPFL’s Doctoral Program in Civil and Environmental Engineering from 2009 to 2017.<ref name="EPFL-people" /> In 2012 he co-founded the European Association for Research in Transportation ('''hEART''') and served as its first president until 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=hEART – European Association for Research in Transportation |url=https://transp-or.epfl.ch/heart/ |website=EPFL |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref>

==Research==
Bierlaire combines discrete-choice theory, operations research and simulation to analyse travel behaviour, design transport policies and evaluate environmental impacts.<ref name="EPFL-people" /> His methods have been applied to public-transport planning, logistics, pedestrian dynamics and land-use modelling. He leads '''Biogeme''', an open-source Python package for maximum-likelihood estimation of discrete-choice models.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biogeme |url=https://biogeme.epfl.ch/ |website=EPFL |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref> Bierlaire created several massive open online courses, including “Introduction to Discrete Choice Models” on edX,<ref>{{cite web |title=Introduction to Discrete Choice Models |url=https://www.edx.org/learn/discrete-mathematics/ecole-polytechnique-federale-de-lausanne-introduction-to-discrete-choice-models |website=edX |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref> and co-teaches the professional course “Discrete Choice Analysis: Predicting Individual Behaviour and Market Demand” with colleagues from MIT and UC Berkeley.<ref>{{cite web |title=Discrete Choice Analysis – Professional Course |url=https://transp-or.epfl.ch/dca/ |website=EPFL |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref>

==Honours and service==
* Founding Editor-in-Chief, ''EURO Journal on Transportation and Logistics'' (2011–2019)<ref>{{cite web |title=EURO Journal on Transportation and Logistics – Past Editors |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EURO_Journal_on_Transportation_and_Logistics |website=Wikipedia |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref>
* Associate Editor, ''Operations Research'' (since 2012)<ref name="EPFL-people" />

==Selected publications==
* Bierlaire, M. ''Optimization: Principles and Algorithms''. EPFL Press, 2015.
* Fosgerau, M.; McFadden, D.; Bierlaire, M. “Choice Probability Generating Functions.” ''Journal of Choice Modelling'' 8 (2013): 1–18.
* Bierlaire, M.; Chen, J.; Newman, J. “A Probabilistic Map Matching Method for Smartphone GPS Data.” ''Transportation Research Part C'' 26 (2013): 78–98.
